clue.text: Some gamble, how a ship may react to rough seas, say

definitions.meaning: a gambling game in which coins are thrown at a mark and then tossed

definitions.text: how a ship may react to rough seas, say
definitions.meaning: a vessel in heavy weather lurches nose up and down and is thrown about

explanation.definitionFit: The name of an old coin-throwing wager also describes literally the plunging and rolling of a vessel in a storm.

clue.text: Old Egyptian gambling game, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the card game's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: faro is an old card game for betting

explanation.surface: Someone describes an ancient betting game from Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Egyptian gambling game' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Old Egyptian'; the card game FARO is spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of ancient Egypt bore this title, so a king of old Egypt fits.

clue.text: One of those up the pole (add 'em up)

definitions.text: One of those up the pole

parts.note: to tot up is to add up a column of figures
taken as written, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside tells someone to total the things carved on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an instruction to count, but 'add 'em up' is TOT 'EM up, with 'up' belonging to the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved emblem stacked on a tribal pole is one of the figures found up such a pole.

clue.text: Ruffians teasing a lion? Gosh!

indicators.note: teasing means pulling apart, so the letters of the words are pulled about

explanation.surface: Thugs bait a big cat, and an onlooker exclaims in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy, violent young troublemakers are thugs or ruffians.

clue.text: With this early navigator at last 13 becomes a pirate

definitions.text: With this early navigator at last 13 becomes a pirate

parts.words: With this early navigator at last 13 becomes a pirate
parts.note: split the Biblical sailor's name into a word of refusal plus an exclamation; then the pipe at 13 having no exclamation at its end leaves Captain Hook, the pirate

explanation.surface: An ancient seafarer somehow turns a numbered thing into a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ark-builder's name splits as a negative and the cry 'ah'; the pipe at 13 with 'ah' removed from its end leaves HOOK, Peter Pan's pirate captain.
explanation.definitionFit: The ark's builder in Genesis steered the earliest vessel recorded, an early navigator.

clue.text: Greek-style quadruped to depart in confusion

indicators.note: in confusion says the letters of the words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A four-legged animal of Greek manner makes a muddled exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists use this Greek-built term for any four-limbed vertebrate, a four-footed creature.

clue.text: Cantonese however is not their regional dialect

definitions.text: Cantonese however is not their regional dialect

parts.words: Cantonese however is not their regional dialect
parts.note: the word for Chinese spoken in Canton sounds as if it should belong to people of cantons, the alpine nation's regions, though it does not

explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is divided into cantons, yet its people speak German, French, Italian or Romansh, not the Chinese tongue.

clue.text: Disheartened trapper upset with case, say, by this comeback

indicators.note: upset means the remaining letters are knocked over and rearranged
disheartened means the middle letter, the heart, of the word trapper is taken out
say signals that the word ease is heard as two letters

parts.note: ease said aloud sounds like E's, two letter Es

explanation.surface: A trapper, downcast and upset, is answered with a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes the middle P of TRAPPER to give TRAPER, which 'upset' rearranges into REPART; 'ease, say' sounds like E's, giving EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty retort, or quick-fire banter, is a clever comeback.

clue.text: Scottish footballers appear kind of cross

definitions.meaning: the Glasgow club that plays at Parkhead
a ringed cross of the early Irish and Scottish church

explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow's green-and-white football club and the ringed cross both take the name of the ancient Gaelic peoples.

clue.text: His journey to a star United Nations organized

definitions.text: His journey to a star United Nations organized

indicators.note: organized means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A space traveller's trip to a distant sun was arranged by the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TO A STAR with UN; the whole clue also describes the space traveller, so 'His journey' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller is the person who would make a voyage toward the stars.

clue.text: One French boy or girl in dire need

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the words dire need

explanation.surface: A French lad or lass is in desperate want.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'One French boy' also gives the name as I (one) plus RENE (a French boy's name), so the girl's name is clued twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, here a girl's name.

clue.text: Somebody's depression a jolly introduction to hell?

parts.note: a Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
the pit is the bottomless entrance to hell, the abyss

explanation.surface: A dip in someone's mood is a cheerful way into the inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like 'cheerful' but is the old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder is a dip or depression in the body.

clue.text: River Arrow's engine part

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge
an arrow is a shaft, the 's here being a link

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the River Arrow is a piece of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arrow is a real English river, which hides that 'River' and 'Arrow' are separate pieces; the Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating rod with lobes that opens an engine's valves is a machine component.

clue.text: Pipe for a rugby player, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the player's position name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a hooker is the forward in the middle of the scrum front row

explanation.surface: A smoking pipe is chosen for a rugby forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the scrum position HOOKER sounds the same as the water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriental tobacco pipe that draws smoke through water is a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Offering to withdraw one thousand dollars from contract

indicators.note: to withdraw means these pieces are pulled out of the word for contract

parts.note: an obligation is a binding agreement
I is the Roman numeral for one
a G, or grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A gift is made in order to pull a large sum out of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrifice or gift presented to a deity is a religious offering.

clue.text: Like Ketèlbey's garden showing no return in gum resin

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the resin's name

parts.note: mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree

indicators.note: return means the word no comes back reversed

explanation.surface: A composer's garden refuses to reappear in a sticky tree sap.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Ketèlbey wrote the light orchestral piece 'In a Monastery Garden'. 'Showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden in Ketèlbey's piece belongs to a monastery, so it is of monks.

clue.text: A pound on at Wyeville for one to beat the Eagle

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
a made-up name for Ross-on-Wye, a market town on the River Wye

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a pound at a Wye town on beating the Eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf an eagle is two under par and an albatross three, so it beats the eagle. Ross-on-Wye is an English town on the River Wye; 'on' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf score of three under par on a hole outdoes the two-under score called an eagle.

clue.text: Bestiary is rewritten by a voluptuary

indicators.note: is rewritten means the letters of the book's title are written out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A medieval book of beasts is reworked by a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: One devoted to luxury and pleasure, after the ancient city of Sybaris, is a voluptuary.

clue.text: Sweet dog Bill Sikes owned

definitions.meaning: a round, hard, striped peppermint candy sold in Britain
the burglar Bill Sikes in Dickens's Oliver Twist owns a bull terrier of this name

explanation.definitionFit: A striped British mint candy shares its name with the bull terrier of Dickens's villain.

clue.text: Darwin's ocean-going hound

definitions.meaning: HMS ship on which Charles Darwin sailed round the world
a small scent hound used for hunting hares

explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's survey ship and a small hare-hunting breed of dog share one name.

clue.text: A black queen first in her order

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
Bess was Queen Elizabeth I's familiar name

explanation.surface: A dark-clad queen leads her religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a sequence but is a religious order; Good Queen Bess was Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: The superior of a community of nuns is the head of her convent.

clue.text: Was contemptuous of the second sort of beef

parts.note: corned beef is salted, cured beef

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the second variety of beef offered.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked down on someone is to have despised or disdained them.

clue.text: This well shows how Descartes' follower lost his head

indicators.note: lost his head says the follower's word drops its first letter

parts.note: a Cartesian is a follower of the philosopher Descartes

explanation.surface: A well demonstrates how a follower of Descartes was beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: A well in which water rises under its own pressure is named after Artois in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore where water is forced up by underground pressure is a kind of well.

clue.text: Took legal proceedings over English kid

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: sued means took someone to court

explanation.surface: Someone went to court over an English child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is kid leather, which suede often is.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather with a napped finish is often made from young goat skin, which is called kid.

clue.text: Endured, say, by company that goes to the wall

indicators.note: say tells us the word for endured is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: stuck it out means endured

explanation.surface: A firm that has endured eventually goes bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the wall' suggests going bankrupt; here it is plaster applied to a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine plaster spread on walls is something literally put onto the wall.

clue.text: Ask for a pin for this surplice

indicators.note: ask for means say the name of the pin you want, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge that fastens machine parts

explanation.surface: Someone requests a pin to fasten a clerical vestment.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking for a cotter pin, you would say 'cotter', which sounds like the short surplice.
explanation.definitionFit: A short white liturgical vestment worn by choristers is a kind of surplice.

clue.text: Secret plan to put money in the kitty

indicators.note: put in places the money inside the kitty

parts.note: the pot is the pool of money in a game, a kitty
L stands for pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A scheme to slip cash into the shared fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy or scheme hatched in secret is a plot.

clue.text: Synonym or antonym of "fast"?

parts.note: fast can mean dissolute, as in fast living, or firmly fixed; one word matches the first sense and opposes the second

explanation.definitionFit: Free-living or immoral matches fast in the racy sense, while slack or unfastened is the opposite of fast meaning fixed.

clue.text: Unusually long title to describe "The Wages of Sin"

indicators.note: unusually means the letters appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An overlong heading is used for a book about sin's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: The wages of sin, in the Bible, are death; here the phrase is read as money gained by wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings from sinful deeds are gained dishonestly, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Abandon one's country to live in seclusion here?

parts.note: to desert is to abandon
an island can be a country, as Iceland or Jamaica are

explanation.surface: Someone forsakes their homeland to live as a recluse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandon one's country' reads as defecting, but a remote isle is also a country of sorts; 'one's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote, uninhabited isle is the classic place to be cut off from everyone.
